# 1. Category Purpose

Category 11 gives the future AI Companion a controlled vocabulary for the
factual fields by which a trader may filter, group, select, or describe Journal
results. It separates identity/provenance, time, price, outcome, direction,
size, sequence, explicit Journal labels, and holding-duration dimensions so a
request such as â€œmy cheap morning losers after two lossesâ€ does not silently
invent a price definition, exchange session, outcome basis, sequence rule, or
trader label.

The Journal Analytics reader remains the authority for server-authorized
user/workspace/account scope, accepted current facts, allocation and round-trip
construction, exact decimals, currency partitions, raw UTC instants,
account-IANA rendering, and visible `ready_closed`, `legitimate_open`, and
`needs_decision` coverage. A dimension can be known to this language inventory
while its capability remains `Planned` or `Unavailable`; that does not make it
queryable through Chat.

This category owns vocabulary for reusable dimensions, not metric formulas,
natural-language date parsing, comparator/ranking grammar, conversation
context, global ambiguity policy, slang, response format, or policy. It never
infers intention, emotion, rule adherence, screenshot existence, plan status,
exchange session, price threshold, or market fact from unrelated evidence.

---

# 2. Category Boundaries

## Included

The controlling inventory covers the exact Section 6 source names for:

- identity, account-isolated provenance, instrument, and raw-record selection;
- calendar/time, session, and externally supplied earnings dimensions;
- execution price and explicitly defined price-class dimensions;
- factual lifecycle state and selected gross/net outcome dimensions;
- lifecycle direction, size, ordered sequence, and duration classifications;
- explicit trader-authored Journal labels, notes, screenshots, plans, and
  review facts.

Every result must preserve its source population and coverage. A selected or
grouped row may not cross an unauthorized account boundary, mix incompatible
currency/timezone partitions, expose a private raw identifier, turn open or
decision coverage into a realized outcome, or use a missing trader/external
fact as a default value.

## Excluded

- Intent routing and requested action: Category 1.
- P/L, outcome, quality, fee, size, time/duration, execution, behaviour, and
  candle metric definitions: Categories 2-10 respectively. Category 11 may
  reference their resulting facts but does not redefine their formulas.
- Operators, comparisons, ranking, inclusion/exclusion syntax, and bucket
  comparators: Category 12.
- Natural-language dates, relative windows, date-range interpretation, and
  timezone wording: Category 13.
- Comparison/ranking, conversational context, terminology/slang, ambiguity,
  response preferences, privacy, and policy: Categories 14-19.
- Writes, manual corrections, protected actions, broker/provider calls,
  external calendar/earnings acquisition, and AI Chat runtime implementation.

## Cross-Category References

- Categories 2, 3, and 5 own the selected gross/net P/L, fee coverage,
  winning/losing/breakeven, and realized-population meanings. Category 11 must
  require a selected compatible basis before using an outcome dimension.
- Categories 6, 7, and 8 own position size, duration/time, exact execution
  role, lifecycle reconstruction, direction construction, and event ordering.
- Category 9 owns behaviour interpretation; sequence dimensions describe a
  factual order only and do not prove discipline, cause, or edge.
- Category 10 owns candle/market-data metrics; price and session dimensions do
  not imply candles, intrabar sequence, exchange calendars, or market replay.
- Later Category 12 owns filtering/comparison operators; Categories 13-19 own
  date/time grammar, ranking, context, terminology, ambiguity, presentation,
  privacy, and safety policy.

# 3. Planning Analysis

## 3.1 Required Planning Questions

1. **What exact problem does this category solve?** It gives factual filter and
   grouping requests one canonical dimension without treating loose trader
   wording as permission to invent facts or definitions.
2. **What canonical concepts belong here?** Only the 111 source-order names in
   Section 4, `C11-DIM-001` through `C11-DIM-111`. They are draft names, not
   locked canonical records.
3. **What related concepts belong elsewhere?** Metric semantics belong to
   Categories 2-10; operator/date/context/ambiguity/policy grammar belongs to
   Categories 12-19.
4. **What data is required?** Server-authorized stable user/workspace/account
   scope; current accepted Journal projections; execution and provenance facts;
   account currency and IANA timezone; coverage/decision state; plus exact
   explicit trader or external facts where a row requires them. For every
   C11-DIM-070 through C11-DIM-082 sequence, the shared contract first fixes
   one server-authorized partition of account, stable instrument, and
   account-local entry date, then builds all current lifecycle candidates before
   analytic filters. It orders first entry by raw UTC then stable round-trip ID
   and keeps `legitimate_open`, `needs_decision`, and incomplete candidates
   visible as unskippable barriers. C11-DIM-083 and C11-DIM-084 instead consume
   the Category 9 daily-rule path for one account-local day.
5. **Which deterministic tools will answer requests?** A future read-only
   Journal Analytics fact-set/query/grouping capability may consume supported
   dimensions. No Chat tool contract is authorized by this draft.
6. **Which concepts are directly observed?** Accepted account/provenance,
   instrument, execution price/time/quantity, explicit Journal label/attachment
   facts, and supplied external facts are observed when present. Raw IDs are
   selection evidence, not broadly listable display fields.
7. **Which are deterministically derived?** Account-local calendar fields,
   price/size/duration buckets, outcomes, direction, sequence ordinals, and
   lifecycle state are derived only from their owning accepted contracts. For
   C11-DIM-070 through C11-DIM-082, analytic filters apply only after fixed
   account-plus-stable-instrument-plus-account-local-entry-date candidate
   construction and cannot renumber a later candidate or remove its predecessor.
   C11-DIM-083 and C11-DIM-084 additionally require the effective Category 9
   saved daily rule/version and its complete daily path.
8. **Which are proxy indicators?** Personal median/recent-baseline size and
   â€œcheapâ€ can be descriptive only when an approved definition exists; none may
   be presented as skill, motive, causation, or advice.
9. **Which are user-labelled?** Setup, strategy, playbook, tag, mistake,
   emotion, rule, ratings, notes, screenshots, plan status, review status, and
   personal session/price/duration/bucket definitions require explicit,
   versioned trader facts where applicable. A covered `custom_tag`, `rule`,
   `rule_followed`, `rule_broken`, or `notes_present` fact is conditional
   evidence only: each remains `Planned` until its language/query contract is
   authorized.
10. **Which are not measurable?** Missing exchange/session/calendar, earnings,
    price-definition, fee, trader-label, screenshot, plan, review, timezone,
    provenance, or decision-resolution facts remain unavailable coverage.
11. **Which terms are ambiguous?** `user`, `account`, `trade`, `price`,
    `cheap`, `penny`, `session`, `winner`, `recovered`, `attempt`, `baseline`,
    `scalp`, `planned`, and `reviewed` require the owning contract or focused
    clarification; no generic synonym is a safe substitute.
12. **What defaults are safe?** Use trusted server-authorized selected scope;
   accepted current facts; account-IANA local rendering from raw UTC; explicit
   gross or net basis; and visible coverage. There is no safe default for a
   price basis: `entry_price` must name either the exact first-opening
   execution/allocation price or a defined quantity-weighted lifecycle-entry
   price. There is also no safe default for a personal threshold/bucket,
   external session/earnings fact,
   trader label, or untrusted identifier.
13. **What requires clarification?** Ask one focused question when the request
    lacks a price basis/unit/currency, gross versus net basis, saved definition,
    date/session convention, account partition, or an explicit trader/external
    fact. Do not ask the trader to recreate missing historic evidence.
14. **What combinations are invalid?** Combining accounts across unauthorized
    scope or incompatible currency/timezone; exposing raw IDs as a broad list;
    classifying open/decision chains as realized; treating broker/import source
   as quality; assigning an exchange session from clock time alone; treating
   gross and net as interchangeable; or deriving labels/intent from prices,
   results, duration, or text absence. It is also invalid to merge the two
   entry-price bases, use a generic entry-price default, construct sequence
   candidates after an analytic filter, skip an open/decision/incomplete
   barrier, omit stable instrument or account-local entry date from a
   C11-DIM-070 through C11-DIM-082 sequence partition, or use
   account-clock/exchange-session fallback for a missing custom session
   definition. It is also invalid to treat a daily-target/daily-loss attainment
   closing event as a later lifecycle start, skip a needs-decision or incomplete
   Category 9 path segment, or rewrite a saved daily rule from a request.
15. **What evaluation coverage proves completion?** Later Sections 5-8 must
    cover every locked source row, scoped and unscoped identifiers, source and
    manual provenance, missing/external facts, currency/timezone partitions,
    ready/open/decision barriers, selected gross/net fee coverage, saved
    definitions, explicit trader labels, negation/exclusion, correction, and
    cross-category ambiguity without inference or privacy leakage.

## 3.2 Dependencies

- **Locked earlier categories:** Category 1 controls intent and coverage
  response; Categories 2-5 control P/L/outcome/quality/fee meaning; Categories
  6-8 control size, time/duration, and execution/lifecycle mechanics; Category
  9 controls behavioural interpretation; Category 10 controls candle/market
  analytics. Category 11 must consume their contracts, not copy them.
- **Journal/module contracts:** one server-derived authorized scope; current
  accepted execution versions and provenance; allocation-conserving round-trip
  projections; `ready_closed`, `legitimate_open`, and `needs_decision` states;
  exact decimal values; trade-currency partitions; raw UTC instants rendered in
  the account IANA timezone; coverage reasons; and privacy-safe output.
- **Explicit/trader/external dependencies:** saved, versioned definitions for
  cheap/penny/scalp/size and duration buckets/custom session; explicit Journal
  annotations and attachment/review/plan facts; an accepted exchange calendar
  or session fact for premarket/regular/after-hours; and an externally supplied
  earnings fact for earnings period.
- **Later dependencies:** Category 12 operators, Category 13 date/time
  language, Category 14 comparison/ranking, Category 15 context, Category 16
  terminology/slang, Category 17 ambiguity, Category 18 response preferences,
  and Category 19 privacy/policy.
- **Unsupported dependencies:** browser/client account identity, raw broker
  identifiers, V3 fallback, guessed currency/timezone/session/earnings data,
  model-created labels, implicit fee completeness, and any broad raw-ID list.

## 3.3 Risks, Overlaps, and Decisions

| Area | Draft decision / risk control |
|---|---|
| Source count | The controller corrected the controlling total to 111. Preserve all 111 listed source bullets in order; no source item is merged or removed. |
| Account and user | Server authorization selects scope. `user`/`account` are never client-asserted filters and raw identity values are not exposed. |
| Raw IDs | `trade_id`, `journal_entry_id`, `execution_id`, and `import_batch` may support trusted exact selection only; no broad enumeration, guessing, or disclosure. |
| Provenance | Broker/import source is factual provenance. It is not a performance, quality, or trust ranking; manual and broker evidence retain their own provenance. |
| Time/session | Store/compare raw UTC; render calendar fields in account IANA. Exchange session labels and earnings periods are unavailable when their accepted external facts are absent. `custom_trading_session` remains unavailable until its saved effective-dated definition states IANA zone, calendar/day applicability, start/end bounds, and overnight handling; there is no account-clock or exchange-label fallback. |
| Price | Every price comparison needs an explicit basis, unit, and currency partition. `entry_price` is either the exact first-opening execution/allocation price or a defined quantity-weighted lifecycle-entry price; never silently merge or default those bases. `cheap`, `penny`, price buckets, custom duration, scalp, and size buckets need a saved definition, never a guessed threshold. |
| Outcome and fees | Winning/losing/recovered dimensions require the owning selected outcome basis. Gross/net cannot be mixed; net requires the Category 5 fee-coverage contract. |
| Population | `ready_closed`, `legitimate_open`, and `needs_decision` stay separately counted. Open or decision rows never become closed, winning, or recovered by inference. |
| Journal facts | Setup, strategy, playbook, tag, mistake, emotion, rule, rating, notes, screenshot, plan, and review are explicit trader facts. Absence is not proof unless a covered explicit presence field supports it. |
| Sequence | Every C11-DIM-070 through C11-DIM-082 sequence unconditionally fixes one server-authorized account + stable instrument + account-local entry-date partition, then builds all current lifecycle candidates before analytic filters and orders first entry by raw UTC then stable round-trip ID. `legitimate_open`, `needs_decision`, and incomplete candidates are visible, unskippable barriers; filters cannot renumber later candidates or remove a predecessor. C11-DIM-083/C11-DIM-084 separately consume the Category 9 daily-rule path: one account-local day, ordered ready-closed closing events, equality-inclusive first attainment, and only later same-day zero-to-nonzero lifecycle starts. The attainment closing event never qualifies as a later start; needs-decision and incomplete path segments are barriers. No rule is rewritten and no sequence dimension infers motive or discipline. |
| Journal status | `custom_tag`, `rule`, `rule_followed`, `rule_broken`, and `notes_present` are `Planned` conditional on a covered versioned fact and later language/query contract. Their underlying conditional facts do not create current Chat support. Other Journal labels and negative states remain unavailable unless later dedicated coverage exists; missing text or silence never supplies a negative fact. |
| Category overlap | Categories 7/8/9 supply metric mechanics; Category 11 supplies reusable dimension vocabulary. Later Categories 12/13 own operators/date parsing, preventing duplicated grammar. |
| Privacy/safety | Never print source filenames, broker account IDs, identity fingerprints, internal UUIDs, HMAC material, or raw identifiers. Return privacy-safe labels/counts/coverage or unavailable status. |

# 5. Canonical Inventory Deliverable

## Batch 1-9 Completion State

Batch 1 contains only `C11-DIM-001` through `C11-DIM-010`, in controlling
order. Capability status is copied exactly from Section 4. A `Planned` record
may rely on conditional deterministic Journal facts, but it is not a current
Chat capability. `Unavailable` has no fallback. No identifier below authorizes
raw-identifier enumeration, display, guessing, or scope expansion.

Batch 2 time records derive local calendar facts from accepted raw UTC instants
and the authorized account IANA timezone. Category 11 owns these dimensions;
Category 13 exclusively owns natural-language date/range wording, relative-date
parsing, and boundary-operator grammar.

Batch 3 retains explicit comparator/bound/overnight semantics for clock-time
dimensions. Named market sessions, externally supplied earnings periods, and
custom trader sessions remain unavailable unless their dedicated facts and
contracts exist. Category 7 owns time/calendar metric mechanics; Category 11
does not choose a generic entry or exit event default for calendar dimensions.

Batch 4 price records retain exact accepted decimals and compatible unit/currency
partitions. They name a price basis before filtering or grouping; no record
creates an FX conversion, generic â€œcheapâ€ threshold, price bucket, or weighted
cost basis by inference.

Batch 5 outcome records retain the declared gross or fee-complete net basis and
the exact `ready_closed` population. `legitimate_open` and `needs_decision`
remain separate factual coverage; no endpoint, candle, or outcome label implies
an intratrade path, motive, cause, or future result.

Batch 6 direction derives from accepted allocation/lifecycle roles, never
Buy/Sell text alone. Size requires a declared basis, compatible unit/currency,
population, and tie rules; it is descriptive only, never performance advice.

Batch 7 sequence records C11-DIM-070 through C11-DIM-082 unconditionally fix
one server-authorized account + stable instrument + account-local entry-date
partition before building all current lifecycle candidates and before analytic
filters. Every partition orders first entry by raw UTC, then stable round-trip
ID. `legitimate_open`, `needs_decision`, and incomplete candidates occupy their
visible, unskippable ordered place; no analytic filter may remove one, renumber
a later candidate, or substitute a predecessor. Outcome sequences require one
declared gross or fee-complete net basis in a compatible currency partition; a
flat, missing/incompatible-currency, incomplete-fee, open, or decision
predecessor is a barrier, never an inferred outcome. C11-DIM-083 and
C11-DIM-084 instead consume the Category 9 daily-rule path for one
account-local day: cumulative selected-basis realized P/L from ordered
`ready_closed` closing events reaches its equality-inclusive threshold first,
then only later same-day zero-to-nonzero lifecycle starts may qualify. The
attainment closing event is not a later start; factually open later starts may
count but supply no P/L, and needs-decision/incomplete path segments are
barriers. Effective saved rule/version/basis/currency are server-selected and
never rewritten from the request.

Batch 8 Journal records use only explicit, covered, versioned facts. Setup,
strategy, playbook, mistake, emotion, and ratings remain unavailable without
their dedicated facts. Tags, rules, factual rule evaluations, and note presence
remain conditional vocabulary, never a source for synonym, motive, outcome, or
text-absence inference. `notes_missing` remains unavailable pending a complete
negative-presence projection.

Batch 9 attachment, plan, and review states require dedicated covered positive
or complete negative projections; silence, missing text, or generic Journal
presence never supplies them. Hold-time records consume only exact Category 7
duration/calendar facts and an explicit saved or application-wide displayed
definition where required. They never apply a colloquial duration default,
silently choose a comparator/equality rule, or recast open or decision coverage
as ready-closed duration evidence.

**Drafted-record status (`C11-DIM-001` through `C11-DIM-111`):** 77
`Planned`, 34 `Unavailable`. These counts are derived only from the drafted
record status fields and reconcile ID-by-ID to the controlling inventory.

# 7. Evaluation Cases Deliverable

Evaluation Batches 1-37 save all one hundred eleven source-order arrays. Each
array has the required 22 ordered case types. The controller accepted the
independent final review of C11-E1 through C11-E111 (2,442 cases). The
evaluation gate is accepted with zero unreviewed or failed cases. This
language-only evaluation work authorizes no Chat route, query, identity lookup,
account switcher, broker connection, FX conversion, venue inference, raw-ID
lookup, date-parser/runtime behavior, or browser/server-local time fallback.
Version 1 is Complete, controller-approved, and locked.

case types: `canonical`, `formal_paraphrase`, `conversational_paraphrase`,

`fragment`, `follow_up`, `correction`, `comparison`, `ranking`, `negation`,
`exclusion`, `multi_filter`, `multi_part`, `ambiguous`, `negative_example`,
`unsupported_data`, `selected_entity_context`, and `cross_category`.
`expectedPrimaryIntent` and `expectedSecondaryIntents` use only locked
Category 1 canonical names. Empty arrays and `null` are explicit.

## 8.2 Scope and Runtime Coverage

The 2,442 saved cases cover server-authorized requester/account scope,
privacy-safe provenance labels, exact accepted trade-currency partitions,
accepted instrument classifications, collision-safe symbols, unavailable venue
requests, opaque trusted lifecycle/entry/execution selection, and covered
import-batch provenance plus raw-UTC, account-IANA/DST-aware exact-date,
date-range, trusted-as-of-today/yesterday, current/prior ISO-week-year, and
current/prior local calendar-month plus current-calendar-year boundaries,
explicit positive local-calendar rolling-day windows, declared stable eligible
lifecycle trade counts, explicit account-IANA one-sided time conditions, and
explicit entry/closing-event account-IANA/DST calendar-quarter and calendar-year
boundaries. Earnings-period classification remains unavailable absent an accepted
attributed external earnings fact/version and effective period. They also retain
custom-session unavailability without a complete effective-dated definition and
the mutually exclusive explicit entry/exit price-basis contracts without current
or candle-price substitution, and exact same-population accepted-execution
min/max/range boundaries with unit/currency, tie, and open/decision coverage,
explicit Category 12 threshold-comparator contracts, and unavailable
complete-versioned-definition-gated price buckets, unavailable approved-definition-
gated penny-stock wording, strict single-currency sub-one Stock classification,
and exact quantity-weighted accepted-opening-allocation entry-cost boundaries,
plus exact ready-closed realized-outcome signs with explicit gross/net basis,
complete compatible net-fee coverage, separate open/decision/incomplete/flat coverage,
and factual positive-residual/open versus final-close/zero-residual/ready-closed state
plus exact ready-closed Category 2 gross-winner coverage.
They retain broker/import-source
distinction, no implicit FX/mixed-currency output, no ticker/venue inference,
no raw-ID list/search/client-ID behavior, no sensitive file/statement/path
output, no invented date/month/year/context, and no browser/server-local time
fallback. They do not add runtime support, authorization, queries, account
selection, broker connectivity, FX conversion, venue classification, instrument
discovery, ID lookup, import history, file access, or date parsing.
